papers.title: Settler's letter
lines: We sailed from Liverpool in the Mimosa in 1865. We were promised green fields. We found a desert.
Then a river, and a future. We planted wheat. We are still here, and we still sing.

papers.title: Tea room menu
lines: Welsh tea in Gaiman: cakes, scones, bara brith, and a pot of tea large enough to float a ship.
Served in Welsh and Spanish and a language of its own, known as Eating.

trail.clue: A tea-room owner buried her takings near the open ground during a flood. 'The river will tell you.'

papers.title: Eisteddfod programme
lines: The Eisteddfod in Gaiman has been held since 1875. Children recite in Welsh, in a country of Spanish.
The adjudicator says 'it is not the language, it is the love'. He is mostly right.

papers.title: Letter from the coast
lines: The penguins at Punta Tombo walk about as though they own the coast, which they do.
I, in my hat, was allowed to stand and watch, provided I looked humble.
